channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Casos Dark Horse e Master: as primeiras pistas de Nunes Marques como presidente do TSE
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, appointed by Bolsonaro to the STF and currently president of the TSE, is the rapporteur in cases concerning the film Dark Horse and Flávio Bolsonaro’s ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro. The PL claims the AtlasIntel poll induced voter responses by including audio of Flávio’s conversation with Vorcaro, while the PT seeks to ban the film over alleged economic abuse. Despite Bolsonaro supporters anticipating favorable rulings, Nunes Marques has indicated a preference for a less interventionist approach in electoral justice.

item.title: Na Parada LGBT+, Erika diz que fim da 6 X 1 veio de travesti preta
item.description: Federal Deputy Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) stated that the progress on reducing the workweek from 6x1 to 5x2 was led by a 'Black trans woman', during her speech at the 30th São Paulo LGBT+ Pride Parade. She linked this labor victory to the presence of LGBT+ people in positions of power, arguing that the community drives change when it occupies institutional politics. Hilton urged the Senate to advance the 6x1 PEC and connected the workers' rights struggle to electoral engagement, echoing the parade's theme: 'the street calls, the ballot confirms'.

item.title: MPF abre inquérito para investigar falhas de fiscalização da Anac
item.description: The Federal Public Ministry (MPF) has opened an inquiry to investigate alleged failures and omissions in the oversight work of the National Civil Aviation Agency (Anac) under the Lula government. The investigation follows a federal budget block of R$24 million, which forced Anac to suspend 40% of its inspection activities, including pilot and flight attendant certifications, aircraft certifications, and technology investments, while also laying off contractors and canceling safety events. Anac warns that these measures directly threaten national air safety, reduce revenue, hinder new professional entry, and block the operation of new aircraft in Brazil.

item.title: Entenda por que o volante Éderson foi convocado para seleção brasileira no lugar do lateral-direito Wesley
item.description: Coach Carlo Ancelotti summoned midfielder Éderson to the Brazil squad for the 2026 World Cup after cutting right-back Wesley, favoring the player's versatility from his time playing on the flank for Atalanta. Éderson, 26, was included in Ancelotti's initial June 2025 list but did not play. The original right-back options considered were Paulo Henrique (Vasco) and Vitinho (Botafogo).

item.title: Quem é Éderson, volante que foi convocado para substituir Wesley na seleção brasileira
item.description: Midfielder Éderson, 26, has been called up to the Brazil national team to replace injured Wesley for the 2026 World Cup. He is a key player for Atalanta, with whom he won the 2023/24 Europa League, and is linked with a move to Manchester United.

item.title: TCU rejeita ação de Flávio Bolsonaro envolvendo ex-nora de Lula
item.description: The Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) dismissed a petition filed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) requesting an investigation into alleged irregularities in the Ministry of Education involving the company Life Tecnologia Educacional. The TCU determined there was insufficient evidence to proceed, rejecting the request based on Federal Police reports that mentioned Carla Ariane Trindade, former daughter-in-law of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

item.title: TCU arquiva ação de Flávio para investigar empresa de ex-nora de Lula
item.description: The Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) dismissed a representation by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) requesting an investigation into Life Tecnologia Educacional, a company linked to Carla Ariane Trindade, former daughter-in-law of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The TCU concluded that the request lacked sufficient evidence, relying mainly on journalistic reports without concrete documents or proof of irregularities, and noted that ongoing investigations by the Federal Police are adequate to address the matter.

item.title: A nova aposta dos bolsonaristas para tentar livrar o ex-presidente da cadeia
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense is seeking to overturn his conviction through a criminal revision action at the STF, claiming weaknesses in the evidence and due process violations, without presenting new evidence. Senator Rogério Marinho, coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, reaffirmed confidence in the former president's innocence, even referencing past statements by Minister Luiz Fux as grounds for hope. Although the case is rapporteured by Kassio Nunes Marques, the bolsonarist strategy revives the 'in Fux we trust' narrative, linking the Vaza-Jato scandal to the current effort to reverse the sentence.

item.title: O lado de Donald Trump na eleição presidencial brasileira
item.description: In less than a week, Trump administration decisions affected Brazil, including designating PCC and CV as terrorist organizations and imposing new export tariffs of up to 37,5%. Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated the apparent Trump support and used it to claim superior security credentials, while Lula accused the Bolsonaro family of treason and revived national sovereignty rhetoric. Despite symbolic gestures, there is no clear evidence that Trump is actively seeking to influence the Brazilian election in favor of any candidate.

item.title: Dino manda retirar vídeo de candidato e critica “bizarrices e grosserias”
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino upheld an order to remove videos posted by Manaus city councilman Alexandre Salazar (PL) targeting former mayor and gubernatorial pre-candidate David Almeida (Avante). Dino criticized the content as containing 'bizarre and vulgar' remarks, emphasizing the need for respect in political discourse.

item.title: Alcione volta ao Maracanã e não desafina na presença de Lula
item.description: Alcione kicked off the 'O Maior Encontro do Samba' tour at Maracanã alongside Zeca Pagodinho and Jorge Aragão, with President Lula visiting Zeca's dressing room escorted by Marcelo Freixo. The show featured Martinho da Vila and announced upcoming special guests: Seu Jorge in Brasília (19/9), Alexandre Pires in Curitiba (7/11), Péricles in Porto Alegre (14/11), and Gilberto Gil in Belo Horizonte (28/11).

item.title: Brasil intensifica negociações para barrar veto da UE à carne
item.description: The Lula government is intensifying negotiations with the European Union to overturn a sanitary veto on Brazilian beef, set to take effect on September 3 and threatening R$9 billion in annual exports. The dispute centers on the EU’s demand for proof of cattle traceability and antimicrobial use compliance, with Brazil assessing whether it can exhaust its reduced-tariff quota before the deadline to lessen economic impact.

item.title: Dino critica 'bizarrices e grosserias' no discurso político e mantém remoção de vídeo com ofensas
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino upheld the removal of an offensive video by councilman Alexandre Salazar targeting David Almeida, labeling it as negative anticipatory electoral propaganda and criticizing the 'colonization of political discourse by bizarreness and vulgarity'. He stated that low-level language is not protected by parliamentary immunity, but allowed the future use of the slogan 'nunca será' in future posts, provided legal and ethical rules are followed, annulling the isolated fine for the expression while maintaining the obligation to remove strictly offensive content.

item.title: Com slogan político, Parada LGBT+ tem profusão de camisas e bandeiras do Brasil: 'país de todas as cores'
item.description: The 30th LGBT+ Pride Parade in São Paulo, held in 2026, centered on the importance of conscious voting and LGBT+ rights advocacy, under the slogan 'The street calls, the ballot confirms'. Participants widely displayed the Brazilian flag’s colors, asserting the national symbol as inclusive and reclaimed from far-right appropriation. Despite reduced sponsorship and fewer sound trucks due to a conservative social climate, the event featured political speeches by figures like federal deputy Samia Bonfim (PSOL) and welcomed first-time attendees from regions such as Belém, Pará.

item.title: Brasil quer convencer EUA de que acordo seria melhor que taxar em 25%
item.description: Brazil is seeking a trade agreement with the United States to avoid a proposed 25% tariff on its exports, arguing that Brazil's average tariff on U.S. imports is only 2.7% and that the U.S. runs a trade surplus with Brazil. The Brazilian government considers a 12.5% tariff agreement unlikely but is working toward a July 15 deadline set by the USTR to reach a deal. Negotiations are complicated by the U.S.'s involvement in multiple global trade talks and the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Lula adota o verde e amarelo às vésperas da Copa
item.description: President Lula posted photos wearing the Brazilian national team jersey at Granja do Torto, accompanied by the phrase 'Brazil belongs to Brazilians,' ahead of the Copa. The post was shared by PT allies and drew comments, including from José Dirceu. The gesture is seen as a symbolic effort to align with national identity ahead of the sporting event.

item.title: Acordo tarifário EUA-Brasil: Governo tenta negociar taxa em 25%
item.description: The Brazilian government is seeking to avoid a proposed 25% additional tariff by the United States on its imports, which it views as interference and protectionism. Negotiations are underway with a new deadline set for July 15 to reach a more favorable tariff agreement, given the U.S. trade surplus with Brazil. Brazil rejects the USTR's claims of unfair trade practices, including criticism of the Pix payment system, and argues its average tariff on U.S. imports is only 2.7%.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: como está o duelo Lula x Flávio após números da semana e às vésperas da Quaest
item.description: Lula has widened his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro following the audio leak involving the senator and former banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master. Recent polls show Lula with 38% in the first round and 45% in a potential runoff, compared to Flávio’s 31% and 40%, respectively, alongside rising rejection of the senator and growth in undecided or blank/null voters. Other right-wing candidates remain unable to break the Lula-Bolsonaro polarization, registering low support.

item.title: Os destinatários do recado de Lula a quem age 'por conta própria' em reunião ministerial
item.description: At the start of last Wednesday's ministerial meeting, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva delivered a public message to aides who, 'on their own, try to take actions in superior courts without consulting the AGU and the Civil House'. The remark, described as a warning about governmental discipline, was published in a subscriber-only article, indicating internal tension over ministers' autonomy in judicial actions.

item.title: Entrosamento entre Lula e Motta vai se estender às eleições na Paraíba
item.description: The rapport between President Lula and Congressman Hugo Motta, observed in recent weeks, will extend to the elections in Paraíba. Nabor Wanderley, Hugo Motta’s father and a Senate candidate for the Republicans, declared his vote for Lula, reinforcing the political alignment between the two families.

item.title: Plano de Lula para industrializar minerais críticos enfrenta fogo amigo
item.description: Lula's plan to industrialize critical minerals faces internal resistance from the Ministry of Mines and Energy and private sector groups like Ibram. The approved Chamber bill, stalled in the Senate, would create a Presidency-linked council to set mineral policy, define critical minerals, and oversee concessions. Critics warn it could centralize too much power and note the U.S. may prefer Brazil's current liberal mining regime, as evidenced by the lack of discussion during Lula's Trump meeting.

item.title: TCU arquiva denúncia de Flávio Bolsonaro em caso de corrupção sobre ex-nora de Lula
item.description: The TCU dismissed Flávio Bolsonaro's complaint against Life Educacional due to lack of concrete evidence of irregularities in FNDE fund transfers to municipalities. The case involved Carla Ariane Trindade, Lula's former daughter-in-law, investigated in Operation Coffee Break for alleged facilitation of fund releases and overpriced textbook sales. The matter was referred to the TCE-SP for evaluation of possible local audits.

item.title: 'A candidatura de Flávio é uma represa rachando'
item.description: Following Donald Trump’s new tariff measures, a sharp political observer likened Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy to a cracking dam — implying structural weakness and imminent risk of collapse under international pressure. The subscriber-only article suggests his campaign faces mounting challenges that could undermine its viability.

item.title: PT escala sobrinho-neto da ex-presidente Dilma para coordenar ofensiva nas redes
item.description: The PT has appointed city councilor Pedro Rousseff, the grandnephew of former President Dilma Rousseff, to coordinate the party's social media strategy for the 2026 election campaign. This move responds to the effectiveness of Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL), who, with 43 million followers, has shaped narratives favoring the opposition and damaging the Lula government. Rousseff, with around 2 million followers, praised for his irreverence and combativeness, has previously served as a government consultant on digital crisis interventions.

item.title: Flávio caça cliques com Tarcísio, mas recebe o vácuo digital do aliado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro turned the March for Jesus into an early electoral rally, sharing photos with Tarcísio de Freitas and Ricardo Nunes, but the São Paulo governor avoided engaging with him on social media, signaling strategic distancing. Tarcísio’s coldness reflects the right-wing fear that a Flávio victory in 2026 would entrench the Bolsonaro clan’s power, blocking alternative plans for 2030.

item.title: PESQUISA PARA PRESIDENTE: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro travam disputa! (05/06/2026)
item.description: A poll released on June 5, 2026, shows a tight presidential race between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and opposition candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. Both candidates are tied in voter intentions, reflecting deep political polarization in Brazil. Although methodological details are not yet disclosed, the economy and security appear to be central issues in the electoral debate.

item.title: PIB perde força e governo Lula tenta conter o estrago com uma enxurrada de estímulos
item.description: Brazil's GDP grew only 2% in the 12 months ending March, the weakest performance of Lula's third term and the worst since 2021, partly masked by government stimulus. Agribusiness (with a record harvest) and public sector consumption were the main drivers, but without them growth would have been just 0.6%. Economists project 1.6% to 2% growth in 2026, with much of it dependent on temporary stimulus measures that do not ensure sustainable expansion.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro e PL querem contrapor PEC da escala 6x1 com projeto de 'trabalho flexível'
item.description: PL and Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign are discussing strategies to counter the PEC ending the 6x1 work scale, proposing a 'flexible work' project as an alternative. The exclusive article highlights behind-the-scenes negotiations in the Senate.

item.title: Alcolumbre dá sinalização sobre da PEC da Segurança
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre is signaling that he may advance the discussion and vote on the Public Security PEC in 2024, despite resistance from the Lula government. He aims to accelerate the legislative agenda following negotiations on the PEC reducing the 6x1 work schedule, provided there is sufficient backing from party leaders. Government allies view the move as a potential obstacle to Lula’s strategic 2026 agenda, including the creation of a Ministry of Public Security.

item.title: PCC e CV estão presentes em mais Estados do que o McDonald’s
item.description: The Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) are present in 25 Brazilian states and the Federal District, surpassing McDonald’s presence, which operates in 23 states and the DF. The U.S. Department of State designated both groups as Foreign Terrorist Organizations on May 28, 2026, following a meeting between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former President Donald Trump; however, experts argue the designation has limited practical effect on combating crime in Brazil.

item.title: Nova taxa é contraditória e politicamente útil aos EUA, diz ex-secretário
item.description: Former Trade Secretary Welber Barral states that the new U.S. tariff on Brazilian products, while seemingly contradictory given Brazil's trade deficit with the U.S., is politically useful for Washington to pressure for access to strategic sectors. The justification shifted from claiming Brazilian protectionism to issues like forced labor, Pix, social media rulings, and deforestation, with no mention of trade deficit or protectionism in the latest report. Brazil does not tax any of the top 10 U.S. products it imported in 2026, while the U.S. taxes 4 of the top 10 Brazilian products it imports.

item.title: Flávio sai ou fica?
item.description: A Noblat Blog poll shows 62.7% of readers believe Flávio Bolsonaro should remain a presidential candidate in 2026, while 37.3% think he should step down. The result indicates a still-loyal base around the Bolsonaro name, despite ongoing controversies involving the senator.

item.title: Idade de Lula não é obstáculo para 67% dos brasileiros, diz pesquisa
item.description: An Indexa poll shows 67.2% of Brazilians believe President Lula's age does not hinder his ability to govern, while 15.5% say it hinders him a lot and 13.7% a little. First Lady Janja released videos of Lula exercising as part of a campaign strategy to highlight his physical vigor and support a fourth term. The Indexa CEO stated that the 2026 election will be shaped more by economy, income, and quality of life than by candidates' age.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pode sufocar na própria cortina de fumaça
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro attempts to deflect domestic scrutiny by pursuing a meeting with Donald Trump in the U.S., using international diplomacy as a smokescreen to overcome the fallout from the Dark Horse revelations. This move unfolds in a highly polarized electoral landscape where both he and Lula enjoy high name recognition but also significant rejection, keeping the race within polling margins of error. The strategy exemplifies the logic of chaos as a political method, driven by digital platforms and the relentless pursuit of audience attention.

item.title: Uma vaga no STF, e as mulheres, de novo, de fora?
item.description: The Senate rejected Jorge Messias's nomination to the STF, marking the first time in 132 years that a government nominee was blocked. Despite a comprehensive list of highly qualified women presented by feminist movements and legal experts, none were considered for the vacancy, continuing the STF's severe underrepresentation of women — only three have served in over a century. This omission reflects a systemic pattern of institutional exclusion, violating Brazil's international commitments under CEDAW and mirroring gender disparities across all branches of government.

item.title: EBC dá prazo para Datena
item.description: The Empresa Brasil de Comunicação (EBC) has given presenter José Luiz Datena until June 15 to decide whether he will run in the 2026 elections. If he chooses to run, he must leave EBC’s TV and radio programs by June 30, as required by electoral law. Datena, affiliated with the PSB, is considering a run for federal deputy from São Paulo.

item.title:
As interferências
na luta eleitoral
item.description: The 2026 election is already being shaped by the political use of religion, with evangelical leaders promoting a 'spiritual war' against evil, as stated by Flávio Bolsonaro. This instrumentalization of faith by politicians and pastors restricts the religious freedom of followers and reflects a Pharisaic attitude, shifting the debate from civic to religious grounds. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Pix e eleições: como o meio de pagamento virou peça-chave da campanha desde 2022
item.description: Brazil's Pix instant payment system has become a central theme in electoral campaigns since 2022, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva emphasizing national sovereignty in its defense and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro crediting its creation to former President Jair Bolsonaro. The political use of Pix reflects its deep integration into Brazilians' daily lives and its ability to shape public perception of the government. The article highlights how the topic has evolved into a tool for ideological and narrative dispute in electoral politics.

item.title: Entrevista: 'Defesa do Pix materializa a soberania, sai do abstrato’, diz cientista político Guilherme Casarões
item.description: Political scientist Guilherme Casarões argues that U.S. attacks on Pix and new tariffs help President Lula turn the defense of national sovereignty into a tangible issue, exploiting Trump’s inconsistent Brazil policy driven by internal U.S. government power struggles. He notes the disjointed nature of the Trump administration, with figures like Marco Rubio promoting a rival stance toward Brazil in Latin America, which allows Lula to offensively defend sovereignty, especially after tariffs and efforts to undermine Pix, reversing the defensive posture previously imposed by Bolsonarist actions.

item.title: Acesso restrito a Bolsonaro gera ruídos na definição de palanques estaduais e gera insatisfação entre aliados
item.description: Despite being under house arrest, Jair Bolsonaro continues to influence strategic decisions in his son Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-campaign, including the definition of state-level electoral slates, with directives relayed through family members. This restricted access has created practical difficulties in verifying information and caused dissatisfaction among allies, who question the authenticity of directives attributed to the former president, although Flávio’s close allies deny any communication issues.

item.title: O custo dos agrotrogloditas
item.description: The text criticizes the U.S. stance toward Brazil, claiming the American government is using arguments about deforestation and the exit from the Soy Moratorium to justify up to 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, despite acknowledging recent environmental improvements. It suggests the real motivation is political, tied to Donald Trump and Flávio Bolsonaro’s efforts to influence Brazil’s 2026 elections, while figures like Johanna Dobereiner and Norman Borlaug represent Brazil’s sustainable agricultural potential. Although the U.S. argument is described as contradictory, it still pressures Brazil to confront the harm caused by irresponsible agro-practices, the 'agrotroglodites'.

item.title: Conheça a linha de crédito para entregadores que será lançada por Lula
item.description: The Lula government is preparing a special credit line for app-based delivery workers, aiming to reduce the costs of acquiring and maintaining motorcycles through financing with lower interest rates and longer terms. The proposal, still under discussion, seeks to break the cycle of indebtedness faced by these informal workers, relying on public banks to make credit more accessible.

item.title: Parada LGBT+ de SP chega aos 30 com apelo às urnas e poucas autoridades
item.description: The 30th edition of São Paulo's LGBT+ Pride Parade takes place on Avenida Paulista under the theme 'Parada SP 30 years: The street calls, the ballot confirms', urging electoral participation. The event occurs without the presence of Mayor Ricardo Nunes and Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, while the federal government is represented by Minister Janine Mello. The parade commemorates three decades of activism for LGBT+ rights and visibility.

item.title: Toribío, el enclave indígena del Cauca que le dio el 92% de sus votos a Iván Cepeda
item.description: Toribío, in northern Cauca, is an indigenous enclave that recorded 92% of votes for the left-wing ticket of Iván Cepeda and Aída Quilcué in Colombia's recent presidential election. Known for its history of enduring guerrilla takeovers in the 1990s, the municipality now positions itself as one of the country's most progressive areas, where supporting the right is socially stigmatized.

item.title: INFOGRÁFICO: Veja os possíveis candidatos de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro nos estados
item.description: The campaigns of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are negotiating state-level alliances for the 2026 elections, focusing on the eight states that concentrate nearly 70% of Brazil’s electorate. These efforts aim to secure strong local slates in São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Bahia, Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul, Pernambuco, and Ceará, where both candidates lead in presidential polls. G1 surveyed the names being considered for state races likely to support each side, though specific candidates are not named in the excerpt.

item.title: 'Não se pode imaginar os escândalos': o Brasil que não passou nas memórias de Wenceslau Braz
item.description: In 1914, Wenceslau Braz was elected president of Brazil without opposition after Ruy Barbosa withdrew, a result of the 'café com leite' political agreement between the oligarchies of São Paulo and Minas Gerais. His victory exemplified the dominance of rural elites in the Old Republic, where electoral competition was virtually nonexistent. The article contrasts this historical context with today’s highly polarized political climate in Brazil.

item.title: Fadiga eleitoral desafia Lula, 80, terceiro governante há mais tempo no poder no Brasil
item.description: President Lula, aged 80, has been using images of his jogging and physical exercise on social media to demonstrate vitality and counter criticism about his advanced age. This strategy, recorded during official agendas and widely shared by his team, aims to reinforce his capacity to govern amid growing electoral fatigue. The content was published on June 6, 2026, at 23:00.

item.title: Caiado diz que governo deixou facções virarem “multinacionais”
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), a pre-candidate for president, criticized the Lula government for lacking 'moral authority' and attributed U.S. tariffs on Brazil to its omission in combating organized crime, stating that criminal factions have become 'multinationals'. He declared opposition to U.S. tariff proposals, both from 2025 and 2026, but noted the current one stems from investigations into unfair trade practices and forced labor, and that Brazil has lost international credibility due to its inaction.

item.title: Jaques Wagner dança “Vai dar PT” com Jerônimo em evento na Bahia
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) danced alongside Governor Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) at a PGP 2026 event in Itaberaba, to a version of the song 'Vai dar PT'. The video, first posted on the Instagram of local vice-mayor Dr. Ramon, drew criticism from the right, including São Paulo councilman Rubinho Nunes (União Brasil), who linked the dance to Bahia's violence. Wagner and Rui Costa are the PT's Senate candidates, while Jerônimo seeks re-election as governor with Geraldo Júnior (MDB) as his running mate.

item.title: PT publica vídeo ironizando aprovações de projetos de Flávio
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) released a video on X mocking the legislative approvals of Flávio Bolsonaro, comparing him to his father Jair Bolsonaro and arguing that, despite image changes, his behavior remains unchanged. In an interview on the 3 Irmãos podcast, São Paulo gubernatorial pre-candidate Fernando Haddad criticized Flávio Bolsonaro's potential presidential bid, stating he lacks the qualifications to hold any elective office due to his ties with Daniel Vorcaro and the Dark Horse film controversy, which Haddad claims undermines any progressive or institutional credibility.
